title: cost-executor: tenant-adaptive defaults, safe quant rollups, unit-econ dry-run
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Large tenants have heterogeneous traffic shapes; applying a single global batching/caching default or a blind quantization rollout can cause unit-econ regressions for latency-sensitive customers. This PR adds a conservative 'cost-executor' safety layer that computes tenant-adaptive defaults, generates safe quantization rollups, and exposes a dry-run mode for unit-economic impact analysis. Motivation: reduce manual tuning, prevent bad global rollouts, and give operators an automated but reversible path for cost-saving presets. Design summary: 1) Tenant-adaptive defaults engine: observes per-tenant request size+latency distributions (past 7d) and synthesizes batch_size, cache_prefix_window, and prefill hints using a rule set with weighted confidence. Defaults are persisted as 'suggested' and can be auto-applied for tenants with high confidence. 2) Safe quant rollups: quant profile generator produces incremental rollup artifacts (Q8->Q4 schedule), each accompanied by a safety checklist including synthetic quality tests and unit-econ simulation. Rollups include precomputed fallback policies for immediate de-escalation. 3) Unit-econ dry-run orchestration CLI: run a simulated pass against stored traces, compute token-cost delta, and produce a per-tenant risk score and recommended guardrails. 4) Telemetry + observability: new events and dashboards to track suggested vs applied defaults, rollup acceptance rate, and unit-econ deltas over time. Rollout plan: merge to main, canary to 5% of tenants for 48h with automatic rollback if unit-econ delta > 10% or error rate increases > 0.5%. Checklist: - [x] Tenant defaults algorithm implemented with configurable confidence thresholds - [x] Quant rollup generator with safety checklist and automatic fallback - [x] Dry-run CLI and CI integration for deterministic runs - [x] End-to-end integration test harness with replayed traces - [x] Console panel for operators to accept/reject suggestions - [x] Documentation and operator runbook added Notes on scope: this PR focuses on the orchestration and safety net; it intentionally does not change the default global policies until canary completes. For big customers where changes are auto-applied, preference is opt-in via tenant flags. Testing strategy: unit tests for the defaults heuristic, synthetic perf/quality tests for rollups, integration tests with the trace-replay harness, and an offline cost-simulator to verify unit-econ calculations. Backwards compatibility: schema changes to tenant defaults are additive and guarded by a feature flag. Migration: a short job converts legacy tenant preference keys into the new suggested/pending model; operators can revert using the console.
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial tenant-defaults engine and tests; add quant rollup generator and safety checklist; dry-run CLI and replay harness; console UI for suggestions; telemetry + helm values for canary rollout.
review_comments: Carlos Nguyen: Can we tighten the confidence threshold for auto-apply? For tenants with <1000 requests/day, prefer manual suggestion. (addressed)
Priya Desai: Rollup generator looks good — add a quality-check that compares top-k tokens after quant to ensure logits divergence < 0.02 for critical prompts. (added in validators)
Liam O'Connor: CI integration for deterministic dry-runs is necessary; ensure the replay harness pins RNG and model seeds. (harness updated)

Maya Patel (author): responded to all comments, lowered auto-apply to 95% confidence for medium tenants and 99% for large tenants, added top-k validation and deterministic seeds, and documented the canary policy in the runbook.
ci_checks: ci/e2e: flaky on first run -> rerun -> pass
perf/regression: no significant regression in 95th latency, token throughput within 1.5%
merge_outcome: merged via squash by Maya Patel after two approvals and green CI. Post-merge actions: canary enabled via helm flag (5% tenants), observability dashboard pinned, and a rollback watch configured for 48h.
release_notes: Add tenant-adaptive batching/cache defaults, safe quantization rollup tooling, and a unit-econ dry-run CLI. Operators can preview suggested defaults in the Console and run simulations before applying. Canary rollout enabled with automatic rollback thresholds.
migration_instructions: Run scripts/migrate-tenant-defaults.sh once after deployment (dry-run first). To revert suggestions, use Console -> Cost Advisor -> Revert. For emergency rollback, disable helm cost-executor canary flag and trigger the rollback script in ops/runbooks.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: global defaults won't change until metrics confirm unit-econ improvement. Quant rollups are stored under /var/lib/redwood/quant-rollups with associated checksum+rollback metadata. Operators should monitor the 'cost_executor.unit_econ_delta' metric during the canary.
user_impact: Low by default; suggested changes are non-destructive. Operators will see new suggestions in Console and can opt to apply them. Tenants enrolled in the canary may experience improved cost per token; we guard against regressions with automatic rollback.
follow_up: Add long-running analytics job to surface tenant cohorts where suggested defaults were repeatedly rejected, and expand synthetic quality tests to include customer-defined prompt sets.
qa_todo: Run replay dry-run on three representative tenant traces (small/medium/large), verify unit-econ estimates vs baseline within +/-3%, and confirm rollback triggers by simulating a 12% cost increase.
